what: Overview: what kind of macros does Arl support?
title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: Arl macros procedural, defmacro-style macros: macro ordinary function receives arguments unevaluated syntax returns new syntax. model used Common Lisp Clojure, opposed Scheme’s pattern-based syntax-rules. top , Arl adds automatic hygiene. Bindings introduced macro body automatically renamed shadow caller’s variables. means simple macros hygienic default – need call gensym every temporary. want intentionally introduce binding visible caller (anaphoric macro), use capture opt hygiene specific symbols. summary: Hygienic default – macro-introduced define, let, lambda bindings automatically renamed. Unhygienic escape via capture – marks symbol hygiene leaves alone, allowing intentional capture. gensym available – generates unique symbols cases need explicit control (e.g. macro-time computation builds binding forms dynamically).

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: macro defined: Macros receive arguments unevaluated – forms passed syntax trees (R calls/symbols), values. macro body constructs returns new syntax, compiler compiles evaluates place original call. can document macros ;;' annotation comments definition (see Getting Started – Documenting functions), use help view documentation REPL:
code: arl> ;;' @description Evaluate body forms when test is truthy. arl> (defmacro when (test . body) arl>   `(if ,test (begin ,@body) #nil)) arl> ;; expands to: (if (> 5 3) (begin (print "yes")) #nil) arl> ;; note that the first `[1] "yes"` is the return value, arl> ;; while the second `"yes"` is the print output arl> (when (> 5 3) (print "yes")) #> [1] "yes" #> "yes" (help "when")

title: Macros and Quasiquote
code: arl> (defmacro double (x) arl>   `(* 2 ,x))  arl> (double (+ 1 2))  ; => 6 #> 6

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: Use . collect remaining arguments list:
code: arl> (defmacro unless (test . body) arl>   `(if ,test #nil (begin ,@body)))  arl> (unless (= 1 2) (+ 20 22))  ; => 42 #> 42

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: Parameters wrapped pair (name default) optional: can mix required optional parameters, combine rest:
code: arl> (defmacro greet ((name "world")) arl>   `(string-concat "hello, " ,name))  arl> (greet)          ; => "hello, world" #> "hello, world" arl> (greet "Alice")  ; => "hello, Alice" #> "hello, Alice" arl> (defmacro opt-rest ((x 1) . rest) arl>   `(list ,x ,@rest))  arl> (opt-rest)         ; => (1) #> (1) arl> (opt-rest 2 3 4)   ; => (2 3 4) #> (2 3 4)

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: Use (pattern ...) destructure macro argument (.e., unpack multiple variables, Python’s x, y = obj): Patterns can nested, defaults, used rest parameters:
code: arl> (defmacro let-pair ((pattern (name value))) arl>   `(define ,name ,value))  arl> (let-pair (x 10)) #> 10 arl> x  ; => 10 #> 10 arl> ;; Nested pattern arl> (defmacro deep ((pattern (a (b c)))) arl>   `(list ,a ,b ,c))  arl> (deep (1 (2 3)))  ; => (1 2 3) #> (1 2 3)  arl> ;; Pattern with default arl> (defmacro with-point ((pattern (x y) (list 0 0))) arl>   `(+ ,x ,y))  arl> (with-point)        ; => 0 #> 0 arl> (with-point (3 4))  ; => 7 #> 7

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: Quasiquote (backtick) primary tool constructing macro output. Inside quasiquoted template, ,expr (unquote) evaluates expr inserts result template, ,@expr (unquote-splicing) evaluates expr (must produce list) splices elements template level ,@expr.

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: Concisely, difference , ,@ , always replaces ,expr one element, ,@, list spliced length greater 1, can replace ,@expr one element.

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: quasiquotes nested, level backtick adds one depth, comma subtracts one. depth-zero unquotes evaluated: useful writing macros generate macros.
code: arl> `(a `(b ,,x))   ; => (a (quasiquote (b (unquote 10)))) #> (a (quasiquote (b (unquote 10))))

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: Arl macros hygienic default. macro introduces bindings (via define macros expand define), bindings automatically renamed collide names call site.

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: Consider swap macro uses temporary variable: Without hygiene, caller variable named temp, macro silently shadow . Arl, macro-introduced temp automatically renamed fresh symbol, caller bindings safe:
code: arl> (defmacro swap (a b) arl>   `(let ((temp ,a)) arl>      (set! ,a ,b) arl>      (set! ,b temp))) arl> (define temp 999) #> 999 arl> (define x 1) #> 1 arl> (define y 2) #> 2 arl> (swap x y) arl> x     ; => 2 #> 2 arl> y     ; => 1 #> 1 arl> temp  ; => 999  (unaffected) #> 999

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: macro function returns expansion, expander runs hygienization pass. pass walks expanded code renames symbols macro introduced (.e. originating call site) binding positions like define lambda parameters. Symbols originating caller’s code marked left untouched. quasiquote expander tags evaluated value origin, marking unquoted caller expressions particular originated containing scope. hygienizer uses tags decide symbols rename.

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: gensym creates unique symbol guaranteed collide user-defined name. Use need create bindings macro-expansion time must conflict: call returns new symbol monotonically increasing counter, incrementing skip symbols already defined.
code: arl> (gensym)          ; => G__N for some N #> G__15 arl> (gensym "tmp")    ; => tmp__N for some N #> tmp__16

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: Arl macros hygienic default, usually need gensym simple temporaries quasiquoted output. gensym useful build forms programmatically expansion time need consistent temporary name across – example, map generates variable number forms must share binding: map builds one define per name, every generated form must reference temporary. forms constructed programmatically rather written directly quasiquote template, automatic hygiene won’t save us: need gensym ensure binding unique. Another common pattern loop macros:
code: arl> ;; bind-all: evaluate expr once, then define each name to the result. arl> (defmacro bind-all (expr . names) arl>   (define tmp (gensym "val")) arl>   `(begin arl>      (define ,tmp ,expr) arl>      ,@(map (lambda (n) `(define ,n ,tmp)) names)))  arl> (bind-all (+ 1 2) a b c) #> 3 arl> (list a b c) #> (3 3 3) arl> (defmacro do-list (binding . body) arl>   (begin arl>     (define var (car binding)) arl>     (define seq (car (cdr binding))) arl>     (define remaining (gensym "do_list_remaining")) arl>     `(begin arl>        (define ,remaining (_as-list ,seq)) arl>        (while (not (null? ,remaining)) arl>          (define ,var (car ,remaining)) arl>          ,@body arl>          (set! ,remaining (cdr ,remaining))))))  arl> (do-list (x '(1 2 3)) arl>   (print x)) #> [1] 1 #> [1] 2 #> [1] 3

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: Sometimes want macro introduce binding visible caller. classic example anaphoric (aif), binds test result fixed symbol /else branches can use . Without special handling, hygiene rename macro’s fresh symbol, making invisible caller. capture builtin overrides : marks specific symbol “intentionally introduced”, telling hygienizer leave alone.

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: symbol – symbol name preserve (quoted). expr – expression occurrences symbol remain unhygienic.
code: (capture 'symbol expr)

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: Usage: capture applied alt expressions (came caller). marks every occurrence inside expressions “introduced” rather “call_site”, hygiene rename . Meanwhile, (let ((,test)) ...) binding macro’s quasiquoted output, capture ensures two sides agree name .
code: arl> (defmacro aif (test then alt) arl>   `(let ((it ,test)) arl>      (if it ,(capture 'it then) ,(capture 'it alt)))) arl> (import display :refer (string-concat))  arl> (aif (+ 2 3) arl>      (string-concat "result is " it)   ; it => 5 arl>      "no result")  ; => "result is 5" #> "result is 5"

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: macro returns quasiquoted expansion containing let ((...)) .... Normally, hygiene rename macro’s fresh symbol. capture walks alt marks symbol origin "introduced". binding references now origin, hygienizer treats belonging scope rename . Without capture, caller able refer :
code: ;; BROKEN -- without capture, hygiene renames 'it' (defmacro bad-aif (test then alt)   `(let ((it ,test))      (if it ,then ,alt)))  (bad-aif (+ 2 3) it 0)  ; it here refers to the CALLER's 'it', not the macro's

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: macro body ordinary Arl code executed expansion time, can perform arbitrary computation returning template:
code: arl> (defmacro const-multiply (a b) arl>   (let ((result (* a b))) arl>     `(quote ,result)))  arl> (const-multiply 6 7)  ; => 42 (computed at macro-expansion time) #> 42

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: Macros can call recursively: Macros can also expand calls macros. expander recursively expands macro calls remain:
code: arl> ;; Thread-first: recursive macro that threads a value through forms arl> (defmacro -> (value . forms) arl>   (if (null? forms) arl>       value arl>       (let ((first-form (car forms)) arl>             (rest-forms (cdr forms))) arl>         (if (list-or-pair? first-form) arl>             `(-> (,(car first-form) ,value ,@(cdr first-form)) ,@rest-forms) arl>             `(-> (,first-form ,value) ,@rest-forms)))))  arl> ;; expands to (- (* (+ 5 3) 2) 1) arl> (-> 5 (+ 3) (* 2) (- 1))  ; => 15 #> 15 arl> ;; when-not expands into unless, which expands into if arl> (defmacro when-not (test . body) arl>   `(unless ,test ,@body))  arl> ;; two levels of expansion: when-not -> unless -> if arl> (when-not (= 1 2) (+ 20 22))  ; => 42 #> 42

title: Macros and Quasiquote
text: Use macroexpand function perform macro expansion expression execution time. macroexpand supports optional depth argument: depth: fully recursively expands macro calls depth = 1 (:depth 1): one expansion step outermost call depth = N: exactly N expansion steps macroexpand-1 convenience alias one-step expansion, equivalent (macroexpand expr 1) (macroexpand expr :depth 1): full recursive expansion, use macroexpand depth (alias macroexpand-): macro? tests whether symbol names currently defined macro:
code: arl> (macroexpand '(when #t 1) 1) ; => (if #t (begin 1) #nil) #> (if TRUE (begin 1) .__nil)  arl> (macroexpand '(when #t 1) :depth 1) ; => (if #t (begin 1) #nil) #> (if TRUE (begin 1) .__nil)  arl> (macroexpand-1 '(when #t 1)) ; => (if #t (begin 1) #nil) #> (if TRUE (begin 1) .__nil) arl> (macroexpand '(when #t (unless #f 42))) #> (if TRUE (begin (if FALSE .__nil (begin 42))) .__nil) arl> (macro? 'when)   ; => #t #> TRUE arl> (macro? 'car)    ; => #f #> FALSE

title: Modules and Imports
text: Arl three mechanisms loading code: load: Evaluates file current environment (source-like; definitions imports file visible caller) run: Evaluates file isolated child environment (definitions imports file visible caller) import: Loads module binds first-class value; use :refer bring exports scope unqualified

title: Modules and Imports

title: Modules and Imports

title: Modules and Imports

title: Modules and Imports
text: load treats argument file path. search stdlib directory — use (import name) stdlib modules. path resolved -: file exists given path, ’s loaded; otherwise error raised.

title: Modules and Imports

title: Modules and Imports

title: Modules and Imports
code: (module name   (export symbol1 symbol2 ...)   body...)  ; Or export everything defined in the module (module name   (export-all)   body...)

title: Modules and Imports

code: ; File: math-utils.arl (module (export square cube)   (define square (lambda (x) (* x x)))   (define cube (lambda (x) (* x x x)))) ; Registers as "math-utils" (derived from filename)

title: Modules and Imports
text: Explicit exports (recommended): Export : Names beginning _ (underscore) private convention excluded export-. lets define internal helpers without accidentally exposing . _ prefix convention applies export-; explicit (export ...) can still export _-prefixed names needed. Re-export imported symbols: default, export-excludes imported symbols. :re-export modifier includes , enabling facade modules re-package multiple modules single name.
code: (module mymodule   (export func1 func2 var1)   (define func1 (lambda (x) (* x 2)))   (define func2 (lambda (x) (+ x 1)))   (define var1 42)   (define private-helper (lambda (x) (/ x 2))))  ; Not exported (module mymodule   (export-all)   (define func1 (lambda (x) (* x 2)))   (define func2 (lambda (x) (+ x 1)))   (define _helper (lambda (x) (/ x 2))))  ; Not exported: _ prefix = private ; Facade module that bundles several modules (module collections   (export-all :re-export)   (import list :refer :all)   (import dict :refer :all)   (import set :refer :all))  ; Users can import everything from the facade (import collections :refer :all)

title: Modules and Imports
text: import special form loads module makes exports available. (import X) binds module environment symbol X. Access exports via qualified syntax (X/sym), use :refer bring specific names scope unqualified. Use :alias module binding.

title: Modules and Imports
text: Symbol (e.g. control): treated module name. Resolution looks stdlib directory first, current working directory. String (e.g. "lib/utils.arl"): treated file path. path-based resolution used (stdlib lookup). path normalized absolute file imported different path strings (e.g. "inst/arl/control.arl" "./inst/arl/control.arl") reuses loaded module.

title: Tail Call Optimization
text: compiler sees (define name (lambda ...)) (set! name (lambda ...)) lambda body contains calls name tail position, rewrites entire function (TRUE) loop. self-call becomes set parameter reassignments followed next, new stack frames allocated. letrec expands set!, means letrec-bound lambdas self-recurse automatically optimized . compiled R code looks roughly like: Temporary variables (.__tco_n, .__tco_acc) ensure new argument values computed parameter reassigned — just like simultaneous let. Unlike Scheme, advanced types tail recursion optimized: - Mutual recursion (f calls g tail position, g calls f). - apply-based tail calls indirect calls higher-order functions. - Anonymous lambdas tail-recurse use fixed-point combinator (name compiler detect self-calls ).
code: arl> ;; The compiler optimizes this automatically arl> (define factorial arl>   (lambda (n acc) arl>     (if (< n 2) arl>       acc arl>       (factorial (- n 1) (* acc n))))) #> <function>  arl> ;; No stack overflow (but 100000! is too large arl> ;; to be representable and overflows to Inf) arl> (factorial 100000 1) #> Inf function(n, acc) {   while (TRUE) {     if (n < 2) {       return(acc)     } else {       .__tco_n <- n - 1       .__tco_acc <- acc * n       n <- .__tco_n       acc <- .__tco_acc       next     }   } }
